name: AIRI brand tokens
note: Source of truth for the AIRI colour, type, spacing, motion and video system. brand.css and everything in templates/ are generated from this file by dev/build-kit/build.py. BRAND.md explains the same values in prose and must agree with it.

rules.note: Three tiers. A tool that applies or checks the brand should fail only on a hard rule and warn on a default. The hard rules cover AIRI-led work; in partner-led work the partner's template sets colour and type, and the logo rule still holds.

hard.rule: Use the logo files as they are: never redrawn, recoloured, stretched or merged with another mark. There is one AIRI logo for all products.
hard.why: it must look the same everywhere

hard.rule: AIRI red is #A32035, taken from the theme, the template or the token. Never approximate it, and never add a red from outside the kit.
hard.why: near-reds are the most common drift

hard.rule: Figtree for all text, with the fallback stack Figtree, Arial, sans-serif. Code may use the monospace stack.
hard.why: one typeface ties the products together

hard.rule: Text meets WCAG AA contrast: 4.5 to 1, or 3 to 1 for large text.
hard.why: people must be able to read it

hard.rule: Colour never carries meaning alone. A status colour comes with a word or an icon.
hard.why: some readers cannot tell colours apart

hard.rule: In data, red never means good, and a red scale never shows a neutral amount.
hard.why: everywhere else in AIRI work red means risk

hard.rule: Nothing flashes more than three times a second, and every video has captions.
hard.why: flashing can trigger seizures, and many people watch without sound

defaults.rule: Everything else in the kit is a default: data palettes, type sizes, spacing, layouts, chart conventions, motion values, video furniture. Follow a default unless a person asks for something different.
defaults.when-a-person-asks: Do what they ask. Do not argue, do not ask for a reason, and do not quietly put the default back later. Speak up only if the request breaks a hard rule: say which one in a line and offer the closest option that keeps it.

gap.rule: When the kit says nothing, reuse the closest pattern the kit already has. If nothing is close, choose the most neutral option. Never invent a new creative treatment.
where-to-look: the components and by-medium sections of BRAND.md
gap.neutral: Ink and greys, Figtree regular, the default spacing, no new colour.
gap.report: When handing the work back, say which gap you hit and what you reused, so the gap can be added to the kit.

color-dark.note: Dark mode overrides, for Claude artifacts and dark tools. Tokens not listed keep their light value. Provisional: computed and contrast-checked, not yet proven in shipped work.

labels.note: The colour of a label sitting on each step: text is ink #1A1A1A, white is #FFFFFF. Every pair is at least 4.5:1; build.py --check enforces it. On a continuous scale, labels are ink on values lighter than the first white stop. Label colours on fills do not change in dark mode.

categorical-policy.status: The slots are a default. Which seven colours fill them is still being chosen; this set is the interim default.
categorical-policy.new-work: New work uses the slot shown for each risk domain.
categorical-policy.existing-work: Existing pages, tools and decks keep their colours. Nothing is retrofitted.
categorical-policy.bypass: A person can set the domain colours aside for one figure, with a reason. For example, they clash with what the figure needs to say.

data.categorical-note: Palette B, 'quiet but distinct', chosen in the November 2026 team review: Paul Tol's muted scheme in the Repository's hue order, chroma capped at 40. Any grouping takes the slots in order from 1. The seven risk domains take slots 1 to 7 by default, in new work only. Slot 8 has no domain.

grade.note: No-red, no-green variant for dense Yes / Partial / No matrices under red chrome.

theme.note: The 12 theme slots shared by PowerPoint, Word, Excel, Google Slides and Google Sheets. Charts made in those tools take series colours from accent 1 to 6 in order: red (the subject), grey (context), ink (a comparison), then category slots 1 to 3. That order suits a chart of one to three series. Charts of named groups are set by hand from the category slots; see BRAND.md section 5.
theme.google-presets-note: Only these four neutrals are Google presets. Ink #1A1A1A, chart gray #898A8D and background #FAFAFA are custom colours. Google's preset named gray is #CCCCCC, the kit's rule, not the kit's gray.

typography.weight-note: 600 is for web and apps only. Slides, documents and figures use 400 and 700.

motion.note: Two registers. ui is for web pages, interactive tools and Claude artifacts: IBM Carbon's productive motion, unchanged. video is for explainer videos and explanatory animation: Carbon's expressive easing and choreography, with one longer step for scene changes. Transitions are conventional. The logo is never animated: it cuts in. Easing values are cubic-bezier control points.

ui.reduced-motion: Honour prefers-reduced-motion: replace movement with a short opacity change, or nothing.

video.transitions: conventional: cards slide on and off with the standard curve, text rises in, scenes cut or crossfade

logo-build.note: The logo is not animated. It cuts in, held still, in video and everywhere else. Chosen in the November 2026 team review (option 5, 'cut') over four 600 ms builds, to keep things simple. The build options are kept in the review record; do not reintroduce one without a new decision.

dropped.note: Square-step transitions, dropped after team review in November 2026. Do not rebuild them.

prohibited: fading, sliding or scaling the logo in

video.note: Fixed furniture for video. Pixel values are for a frame whose short side is 1080 px.

vertical.use: phone feeds; design it again, do not shrink the landscape cut

square.use: feeds that crop to a square

grid.note: Layout grid for video, built on the squares of the icon. The module is the icon's small square, set to 1/27 of the frame's short side, so the large square (3 modules) tiles every format exactly.

length.rule: Under a minute; shorter is better. Most explainers land between 30 and 60 s. Cut scenes before speeding up the voice.

narration.voice-style: clear, warm, brisk; conversational, never slow
narration.rule: Write about 140 words for a 55 s video. People can speed up; nobody should have to.

music.style: When wanted: a sparse ambient bed, soft piano or warm pads, 70 to 90 bpm, no vocals, no drums or percussion, no build-ups or drops.
music.level: At least 15 LU under the voice; the renderer sets it
music.rule: Off by default, because people watch explainers sped up and music sounds wrong at 1.5x or 2x. Use it for a title sequence, a trailer or an event loop, and say it was generated.

captions.size-rule: at least 1/20 of the frame's short side
captions.srt: An SRT file ships with every video.

lower-third.place: bottom left, inside the title-safe area; never over a face or a caption

video.alternative: A static key frame and a transcript accompany every video.

decisions.note: What the team review of November 2026 settled, and what is still open. Open items keep an interim default; follow it until the item closes.

decided.decision: Red. Section slides are full red.
Conventional. The square-step wipe and the stepped title reveal are dropped.
None. The logo cuts in. Chosen over four 600 ms builds to keep things simple.
One set, as a default for new work only. Existing work is never retrofitted. A person can set it aside for one figure, with a reason.
Palette B, 'quiet but distinct': eight colours in a fixed order for any grouping. The seven risk domains take slots 1 to 7.
Colour a grouping only when the colour says something. Bars that compare groups are one colour. Up to eight groups take the slots in order; more than eight are grey with direct labels.
One colour, one job. A comparison series is ink, not blue. Blue shades counts; a flat blue is a category colour.

open.text: Dark values are defined in brand.css and the artifact template. They pass contrast checks but have not been proven in shipped work or on a projector. Treat them as provisional.
AIRI red has not been matched to a print ink. One proof is needed before the next printed report.
The kit has no rules for imagery yet. Report covers use one white line texture each on red. Whether each product should have its own motif is undecided.

open.topic: Template files for Slides, Docs, PowerPoint and Word
open.text: The kit ships theme colours, fonts and style tables. Finished template files built from them (a slide deck with layouts, a document with page furniture) are still to come.

not-airi.note: Reds that belong to other marks. They stay inside their own logos.

avoid.note: Tool defaults that cause drift. Never pick these.

replaced.note: Values that no longer exist, and the token that replaces each: kit 1.x values, and the kit 2.0 draft category colours replaced by palette B in November 2026.

deprecated.note: CSS variable names from kit 1.x. brand.css keeps them as aliases so old code still works. Do not use them in new work. A value that is not a token name is kept as written. The tokens.json keys themselves are gone: color.dark (now color.text), typography.size.3xl, typography.line-height.relaxed, radius.lg and radius.full; scripts that read them must change.
